annotations.title: CPR deadline calculator (CPR 2.8 clear days and time limits)

description: Works out a deadline under the Civil Procedure Rules in England and Wales from a date: clear days (CPR 2.8(2) and (3)), the 5-day rule (CPR 2.8(4)), calendar months (CPR 2.10), court office closures (CPR 2.8(5) and PD 2A) and the latest days to email or post a document for deemed service (CPR 6.26). Name a common time limit as a preset (for example the defence, the acknowledgment of service, the appellant's notice or Points of Dispute), or give your own period, plus the date it runs from.

act.description: Without a preset: "court" for a filing at court (default), "serve" for a document to be served, "other" for anything else.

amount.description: Without a preset: the length of the period, e.g. "14".

direction.description: Without a preset: "within" a period after the event (default), at least a period "before" it, or at least a period "after" it (gives the earliest day).

event.description: The date the period runs from: the date of service, of the decision, of the hearing or other event (YYYY-MM-DD).

preset.description: A common time limit (the enum lists them all). Where the id is not self-explanatory: defence-14 = no acknowledgment filed; defence-28 = after an acknowledgment; reply-to-defence = earliest date the court can set; defence-28-extended = CPR 15.5; agreed-extension = CPR 3.8(4); costs-budget = Precedent H; budget-discussion-report = Precedent R; statement-of-costs-fast-track = fast track trial; part-36-relevant-period = 21 days; notice-of-commencement = N252; replies = to Points of Dispute; request-assessment = N258; costs-officer-appeal = from an authorised court officer. Leave "" to give your own period.

unit.description: Without a preset: "days" (default) or "months" (months only for a period after the event).
